source_text: Sed ad hoc nos referimus. Et illud ergo aliud, quod paribus momentis appenditur fieri profitere, id est ut iustitiae parentum filiis suis prosint eosque sanctificent atque illis tantummodo non dicantur prodesse, qui grandioris iam aevi natales iustitias propriis attrivere criminibus, ut, quia utrumque a Deo negatum et alterum alterius exemplo dissertum atque inculcatum est, quam tu negationem rationibus tuis videns esse contrariam in parvulis mentitam esse contendis, ambas eius partes nascentium conditione confutes. Quod cum feceris, duo mala pariter perpetrabis, unum, quod oppugnat sententiam Dei, aliud quoniam nasci de iusto iustum et de criminoso asseris criminosum.
pass_a_gloss: But to this we refer ourselves. Confess therefore also that other thing, which is hung by equal moments, to happen, that is that parents' justices profit their sons and sanctify them, and are said not to profit only those who already of greater age have worn away natal justices by own crimes, so that, because both have been denied by God and each has been discoursed and impressed by the example of the other, which denial you seeing to be contrary to your reasons contend in little ones to have been a lie, you refute both its parts by the condition of those being born. Which when you have done, you will perpetrate two evils equally, one which attacks the sentence of God, another since you assert that a just one is born from a just and a criminal from a criminal.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis

pass_b_english: Here is our reply. Then admit that the other proposition, which carries equal weight, also holds: parents’ righteous deeds benefit and sanctify their children, and fail to benefit only those who, once older, have worn away their inborn righteousness by their own crimes. God denied both propositions, explaining and repeatedly emphasizing each through the example of the other. Since you see that his denial opposes your reasoning and insist that it is false concerning infants, refute both its parts by the condition of newborn children. When you do so, you will commit two evils together: you will attack God’s pronouncement, and you will assert that a righteous person is born from a righteous person and a criminal from a criminal (Ezekiel 18:19–20).

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Explicitly discusses the prophet’s pronouncement on personal righteousness and guilt rather than inherited guilt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
